headline: Automated pipelines integrate transcriptomic evidence to annotate eukaryotic genomes
label: Eukaryotic Genome Annotation Pipelines
summary: Recent work integrates RNA-seq and homology evidence into annotation and orphan-gene classification tools for divergent and microbiome genomes.
synthesis: The dominant thread is evidence integration for gene identification. OMAnnotator repurposes the OMA orthology algorithm to merge ab initio, transcriptomic and homology predictions into a consensus eukaryotic genome annotation. Eukan similarly combines RNA-seq evidence with consensus weighting and post-annotation recovery for less studied and divergent eukaryotes. nf-core/proteinfamilies addresses scale as an open-source Nextflow pipeline that generates protein families or assigns new sequences to existing ones. A gut metatranscriptomics preprint applies XGBoost over 154 features to separate expressed orphan genes from spurious and conserved genes, with AUC 0.82 and 0.93. What is new is the combination of orthology inference and transcript-level evidence within automated workflows.
